summary: One constrained, fixed-weight engineering hypothesis is proposed for human review. This is a one-shot BSD100 holdout evaluation of horizontal-flip self-ensemble, an existing inference method, with no claim of novel science or broader research competence. The planner request's account usage and USD cost are unknown and are not included in the experiment proxy budget.
rationale: Horizontal-flip ensemble is the smallest supported intervention with a direct paired comparison and no degradation-model mismatch. It tests whether averaging the original and flip-inverted predictions produces an adoption-relevant PSNR-Y gain while remaining inside the predeclared latency guard. A negative valid result stops this intervention; parameters, metrics, thresholds, sampling, trial count, weights, and architecture must not be changed to rescue it.

protocol.hypothesis: For fixed official SwinIR-S x2 weights, horizontal-flip ensemble increases BSD100 mean per-image PSNR-Y by at least 0.05 dB over unensembled full-image inference, has a strictly positive 95% paired bootstrap lower confidence bound, and keeps aggregate latency at or below 2.5 times baseline latency.
protocol.baseline: Fixed official SwinIR-S x2 DIV2K checkpoint at source revision 6545850fbf8df298df73d81f3e8cba638787c8bd, using full-image inference with no ensemble or tiling.
controlled_variables: Official SwinIR-S x2 checkpoint and source revision
All 100 frozen original BSD100 x2 image pairs
Metric implementation and per-image PSNR-Y aggregation
No training, new weights, architecture changes, tuning, sweeps, case selection, cropping, filtering, or shuffling
Float32 averaging before clamping or rounding
One unscored small warmup per arm, included in compute accounting
Alternating arm order across the frozen observation list
Reporting of storage byte-hours, peak memory, inference latency, and aggregate candidate-to-baseline latency ratio
validity_checks: All 100 frozen BSD100 image pairs evaluated
Frozen inputs and metric code unchanged

outcomes.go: CONTINUE to adoption review only if the mean paired PSNR-Y gain is at least 0.05 dB, the 95% paired bootstrap lower bound is greater than 0 dB, and the aggregate latency ratio is at most 2.5. This eliminates the hypothesis that the intervention fails the predeclared pilot quality, uncertainty, or latency criteria.
outcomes.stop: STOP horizontal_flip_ensemble if the measurement is valid and any GO condition fails. This eliminates this fixed intervention as an adopted route under the declared threshold and constraints; do not adjust parameters, metric, threshold, sampling, number of trials, weights, or architecture. A fresh route requires genuinely new external evidence.
outcomes.invalid: Do not interpret an operational or validity failure as evidence against the hypothesis. Record the specific measurement failure and its correction before proposing a new protocol; no automatic retry is authorized.

evidence.claim: G0 reportedly reproduced Set5 PSNR-Y of 38.1394098 versus a reference value of 38.14; this supports implementation consistency only and is not evidence for the candidate intervention.
The official EDSR repository reportedly describes self-ensemble inference as an existing engineering method.
The SelfExSR repository reportedly supplies standard bicubic LR/HR benchmark pairs.
All 100 BSD100 x2 pairs were reportedly downloaded and hashed before planning, and no BSD100 measurements were obtained.

assumptions: The supplied checkpoint, source revision, frozen observations, and metric code are available and internally consistent; this planner did not verify them.
The 0.05 dB minimum effect is a predeclared pilot adoption threshold, not a validated customer-value threshold.
Seed 0 is an execution identifier only; deterministic inference is not treated as randomized training evidence.
Bootstrap resampling is over the 100 original images, never patches or repeated inference runs.

The experiment proxy budget covers the declared local execution proxy only. Unmetered setup, electricity, hardware depreciation, subsequent retention, storage pricing, and the planner request's account usage and USD cost remain unknown.
Public benchmark data are not guaranteed unseen to the language model and are not access-isolated.
risks: Horizontal-flip ensemble requires exactly two forward passes, so it may fail the aggregate latency guard despite improving PSNR-Y.
The one-shot holdout design permits no development measurement or candidate selection after observing BSD100 results.
Timing is descriptive and is not a multi-run production latency benchmark.
Storage byte-hours, peak memory, inference latency, and excluded real-world costs must be reported; missing resource accounting invalidates cost interpretation.
Dataset provenance and source claims are unverified and require human review.
A valid negative result stops only this constrained intervention under this protocol; it does not establish a general scientific claim about self-ensemble or super-resolution.
